data.name: Jagapathi
data.gender_notes: Jagapathi is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Jagat refers to the universe and Pati means Lord. Therefore, Jagapathi translates to 'Lord of the Universe'. This name is associated with the Hindu deity Shiva, who is often referred to as Mahadeva, the Great Lord. The name Jagapathi carries the meaning “Lord of the Universe” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Jagapathi usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the universe and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes power, strength, and control over the universe.
data.etymology: Jagapathi belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of the Universe.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jagapathi total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

historical_references.reference: Jagapathi Swami I (972-1022 CE), also known as Saranga Swami or Panchanada Swami, was a famous Vaishnavite saint and philosopher in medieval India. He is believed to have composed works like the 'Jagadguru Tarangini' and 'Jeevan Sangha'. His teachings greatly influenced the Bhakti movement in India.
historical_references.context: Medieval India, Vaishnavite saint and philosopher

historical_references.reference: Jagapathi Raju (1779-1855 CE), also known as Ramachandra Raju, was a Zamindar (landlord) of the Rayalaseema region in the British Indian province of Andhra Pradesh. He played a significant role in the Indian independence movement. He was one of the leaders of the Sepoy Mutiny in 1857, which marked the beginning of the Indian independence struggle against British rule.
historical_references.context: British Indian province of Andhra Pradesh, Indian independence movement, Zamindar

Lastly, on YouTube, a variety of videos, including devotional hymns, spiritual discussions, and self-help tutorials, feature the name Jagapathi prominently.
